recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should avoid re-adding item.type to the automatically derived-values list; broader definition-driven Questionnaire processing should continue to follow the already-applied FHIR-28305 and SDC guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-13900 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked to resolve the apparent conflict between Questionnaire.item.definition saying values such as type could be inferred from an ElementDefinition and Questionnaire.item.type being mandatory. The accepted resolution was to clarify inference language so type, required, and similar values can still be inferred or compared while required Questionnaire elements remain specified on the Questionnaire instance.
initial_application: The issue was applied by a55b9bbe29675c4946a1b1f41615c45f8567e12e, which changed source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml to say that Questionnaire-provided information overrides the definition and that some elements are always required to be populated so invariants can be enforced.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. Later published work in FHIR-28305 removed item.type from the derived-values list and added the current explicit statement that Questionnaire.item.type corresponds to ElementDefinition.type but is mandatory and cannot be populated from item.definition. FHIR-28305 is already represented on the combined branch. Current StructureDefinition source keeps Questionnaire.item.type as 1..1 and says it must be present and should align with ElementDefinition.type if a definition is referenced. FHIR-15883 later refined the item.definition URI syntax and examples without changing the seed's accepted inference clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active Questionnaire narrative and StructureDefinition already satisfy the FHIR-13900 resolution and do not contain the original misleading implication that mandatory item.type can be omitted and filled solely from item.definition.
